item.title: Chevron, Shell near first major Venezuela oil deals since Maduro's capture
item.description:
Chevron and Shell are closing in on the first major oil production agreements with Venezuela since the U.S. military captured President Nicolás Maduro in January, according to a Reuters exclusive citing five sources close to the negotiations.

The deals would allow both companies to expand output in some of Venezuela's most coveted oil regions, marking the most concrete steps yet toward what President Donald Trump has described as a $100 billion effort to rebuild the country's battered oil sector after decades of mismanagement under Maduro and his predecessor Hugo Chávez.

item.title: Witkoff likely to visit Israel next week to coordinate Iran war plans
item.description:
White House special envoy Steve Witkoff said Tuesday that he will likely travel to Israel next week alongside Jared Kushner to coordinate military strategy with Israeli leaders as the US-led campaign against Iran enters its second week.

In a CNBC interview on March 10, Witkoff said the United States has "destroyed almost all of their enrichment capability and conversion capability," while acknowledging that Iran's nuclear program has not been entirely eliminated. He added that Iran has shown no interest in returning to negotiations since the US and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury on February 28.

item.title: US destroys 16 Iranian mine-laying vessels near Strait of Hormuz
item.description: U.S. Central Command said American forces eliminated 16 Iranian mine-laying vessels near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, escalating a confrontation over the waterway that carries roughly 20 percent of the world's daily oil supply. The strikes came as Iran's Revolutionary Guards vowed to block all oil exports from the region for as long as the war continues.

item.title: Iran begins laying mines in Strait of Hormuz, CNN reports
item.description:
Iran has begun laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's crude oil passes, according to CNN, citing two people familiar with U.S. intelligence. The move deepens a supply crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran that began on February 28, leaving an estimated 15 million barrels per day of crude oil production and additional refined fuel stranded in the Persian Gulf.

The mining operation remains limited so far, with only a few dozen mines deployed in recent days, but Iran retains the capacity to lay hundreds more. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has warned that any ship attempting to transit the strait would face attack, effectively rendering the passage closed since the conflict's start.

item.title: Iran deploys naval mines in Strait of Hormuz, US intelligence says
item.description:
Iran has begun deploying naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes, according to U.S. intelligence, a dangerous escalation that threatens to deepen the blockade of the world's most critical energy corridor just as Washington's credibility on reopening it suffered a blow on Tuesday.

Small Iranian craft capable of carrying two to three mines each have been detected moving into the waterway, CBS News senior White House reporter Jennifer Jacobs reported on X, citing reporting by Jim LaPorta. While Iran's total mine stockpile is not publicly known, estimates over the years have ranged from roughly 2,000 to 6,000 naval mines of Iranian, Chinese, and Russian-made variants.

item.title: Macron to convene G7 leaders call on Iran crisis, energy prices
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron will convene a call with Group of Seven leaders on Wednesday to address the Iran crisis and soaring energy prices, his office announced on Tuesday, as governments scramble to contain the economic fallout from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

The leaders' call comes after G7 energy ministers met earlier on Tuesday but stopped short of agreeing to release strategic oil reserves, instead asking the International Energy Agency to assess the situation before acting. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol responded by convening an extraordinary meeting of the agency's member governments to evaluate "current security of supply and market conditions" and determine whether to make emergency stocks available.

item.title: US Navy refuses escort requests through Hormuz
item.description: The US Navy has refused near-daily requests from the shipping industry for military escorts through the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran on February 28, telling industry leaders the risk of attacks remains too high, according to a Reuters report citing three shipping industry sources familiar with the matter. The refusal stands in sharp contrast to President Donald Trump's repeated assurances that the Navy stands ready to escort tankers through the waterway whenever needed.

item.title: IRGC says Iran will decide when war ends, threatens Gulf oil blockade
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Tuesday dismissed President Donald Trump's assertions that the US-led war against Iran was nearing its end, declaring that Tehran — not Washington — would determine when the conflict concludes. The sharp rebuke came alongside a threat to halt all oil exports from the Persian Gulf, raising the specter of a prolonged disruption to global energy markets.

item.title: Half of Iran's missiles carry cluster warheads, IDF says
item.description:
Roughly half of the approximately 300 ballistic missiles Iran has launched at Israel since the war began on February 28 have carried cluster bomb warheads, the Israel Defense Forces disclosed on Tuesday, as the deadly munitions claimed two more lives in central Israel.

The cluster warheads explode at high altitude, dispersing dozens of smaller bomblets — each containing several kilograms of explosives — over a radius of about 10 kilometers, according to the IDF Home Front Command. The weapons pose a particular challenge because the scattered submunitions are difficult for air defense systems to intercept once they separate from the main missile body.

item.title: Trump administration asks Israel to halt strikes on Iran's oil infrastructure
item.description:
The Trump administration on Monday asked Israel to stop conducting strikes on Iranian energy facilities, marking the first time Washington has sought to restrain its ally since the two nations launched their joint military campaign against Iran on February 28, according to Axios.

The request came after Israeli warplanes struck at least 30 fuel storage facilities in and around Tehran on Saturday night, igniting massive fires that blanketed the Iranian capital in toxic black smoke and triggered warnings of acid rain for the city's 10 million residents. The strikes represented the first Israeli attacks on Iran's energy infrastructure since the war began.

item.title: Iran launches drone strikes on Haifa refinery in second attack in three days
item.description:
Iran's military announced Tuesday that it launched drone strikes against Israel's oil and gas refinery and fuel storage facilities in the northern port city of Haifa, marking the second Iranian attack on the facility in three days and a deepening of the energy infrastructure war between the two countries.

"Iran's Army Air Force launched suicide drones targeting oil, gas, and fuel storage facilities of the Israeli regime in Haifa in response to attacks on Iran's oil depots," the spokesman for the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, the unified command of Iran's armed forces, said in a statement carried by Iranian state media. The Haifa refinery, operated by the Bazan Group, is Israel's largest oil-processing facility, with a capacity of 197,000 barrels per day. It had reportedly shut down several units last week as a precautionary measure.

item.title: Merz calls Israel's West Bank settlement push a 'big mistake'
item.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Tuesday sharply criticized Israel's settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, describing the moves as "annexation steps" and calling on the Israeli government to reverse course. Speaking at a joint press conference with Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš in Berlin, Merz warned that advancing the so-called E1 settlement project would "further complicate the two-state solution."

"I want to be clear here," Merz said. "The annexation steps discussed in Jerusalem will further complicate the two-state solution." He added that the German government "urgently demands the abandonment of such steps" regarding the E1 area, calling the project "a big mistake."

item.title: Jurists accuse Bukele's government of crimes against humanity
item.description:
A group of international legal experts filed a formal complaint with the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights on Tuesday, accusing El Salvador's government of committing crimes against humanity during its four-year state of emergency. The 275-page report represents the most serious accusation of human rights violations leveled against President Nayib Bukele's administration since he took office in 2019.

The complaint, filed by the International Group of Experts for the Investigation of Human Rights Violations under the State of Exception in El Salvador — known by its Spanish acronym GIPES — alleges there are "reasonable grounds" to conclude that crimes against humanity, as defined by Article 7 of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, are taking place in the Central American nation. The report contends that the violations stem from a state policy "known and even promoted by the highest levels of President Nayib Bukele's government."

item.title: Trial opens for 4 men charged in Haiti president's assassination
item.description: Prosecutors told a Miami jury on Tuesday that greed, arrogance, and a thirst for power drove four men to conspire in the 2021 assassination of Haiti's last democratically elected president, Jovenel Moïse, in a case that has taken nearly five years to reach trial.

item.title: IEA proposes largest-ever oil reserve release amid Hormuz crisis
item.description:
The International Energy Agency has proposed the largest emergency release of oil reserves in its history, surpassing the 182 million barrels released in two batches during the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022, as disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz threaten to upend global energy markets. The proposal, first reported by The Wall Street Journal, was circulated during an extraordinary meeting of IEA member governments on Tuesday, with countries expected to decide by Wednesday — and adoption assured unless even one member objects.

The move comes as the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, which began with joint strikes on February 28 under Operation Epic Fury, has effectively shut down the world's most critical oil chokepoint. Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — which normally carries roughly 20% of global waterborne crude — has ground to a near halt, with maritime intelligence firm Windward reporting just two outbound Iranian-flagged transits and no inbound crossings on March 8.

item.title: IEA to hold emergency meeting as Iran war roils energy markets
item.description: The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, now in its eleventh day, has upended global energy markets and reignited debate over whether the world's dependence on fossil fuels can survive another geopolitical shock. With oil prices surging more than 24% and roughly 20% of global crude and natural gas supply suspended, some experts and world leaders say the crisis makes the strongest case yet for accelerating the transition to renewable energy — while skeptics warn the moment may pass as quickly as it arrived.

item.title: New AI tools compress months of drug and protein research into days
item.description: A wave of new artificial intelligence tools is reshaping how scientists study gene regulation, decode protein structures, and synthesize drugs, with several studies published in recent weeks demonstrating that machine learning can compress years of laboratory work into days.

item.title: Gold edges higher ahead of key CPI release amid Iran war
item.description: Gold prices rose in early trading on Wednesday as investors balanced ongoing geopolitical risks from the U.S.-Iran war against anticipation of a key inflation report due later in the day. The precious metal climbed to around $5,205 per troy ounce on March 11, gaining 0.31% from the previous session, according to Trading Economics.

item.title: Asian stocks rally as IEA mulls record oil reserve release
item.description: Global stock markets lurched through another volatile stretch as investors grappled with conflicting signals about the trajectory of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in its 11th day. Asian equities extended gains on Wednesday while oil prices stabilized after reports that the International Energy Agency was considering a record release of emergency crude reserves.

item.title: Spanish researchers develop artificial cornea from fish scales
item.description: Scientists at Spain's University of Granada have developed an artificial cornea made from fish scales commonly found at local markets, offering what could become a cheaper alternative to donor transplants for patients with severe corneal disease.
